elements.text: Failure of the captain to use proper directional control techniques to maintain the airplane on the runway
Captain failed to compensate for moderate crosswinds from the right
Airplane weathervaned and drifted off the right side of the runway
Minimal rudder commands used by the captain
Inappropriate tiller nosewheel steering commands used by the captain
Lack of forward pressure on the control column by the captain
Procedural shortcomings in air traffic control prevented timely provision of windshear advisory information
Practice of displaying only centerfield wind on LLWAS limited controller information
Airplane was within weight and balance limitations
Flightcrew was properly certificated and rested
Flightcrew training records met FAA standards but were inadequate for trend analysis
LLWAS system operated within acceptable limits
Weather information provided to flightcrew was timely and accurate
Wind gusts recorded on centerfield anemometer were not a factor
No microbursts or hazardous low level windshears affected the airplane
Line of moderate to heavy showers and thunderstorms was crossing the runway
Evacuation was handled expeditiously despite difficulties
Emergency lighting did not operate properly due to out-of-sequence battery packs
Manufacturer's instructions did not describe importance of sequencing batteries
Runway was worn to maintenance planning level but friction was within guidelines
Inadequate FAA oversight of runway friction measurement
Emergency response of DFW ARFF was exceptionally good
No evidence of hydroplaning or reverted rubber
Broken nose landing gear steering cables were a result of the accident, not a cause
Two reverser cascades were not in proper configuration
